gap: Acceptance check for A: a single directional sun gives every visible tower a clearly lit face and a clearly darker shadow face (at least about 30% luminance difference), with cast shadows visible on the ground and water. The skyline loses contrast and saturation with distance in at least three readable depth layers. The rotor renders as motion-blurred blade streaks around a visible hub, with no solid ring or halo.

Judge: B is clearly better in all four pairs, and none of them was close. I judged only the rendered scenes. The B frames are clean beauty shots with no HUD and a publisher logo watermark, and the A frames show gameplay HUD; I discounted both overlays, and every verdict holds without them. The B frames get their quality from strong lighting design: a low sun or dusk key light, aerial haze that builds clear depth, and believable materials (gloss paint, glass, fabric, water spray). Their dynamic, staged compositions make the helicopter or the character the clear hero. The A frames come from one recognisable harbour city, and they do have a coherent palette, legible landmark massing, and boats with wakes that add some life. Every A frame shares the same problems. 1) Lighting is flat and mostly ambient, with weak value structure and little falloff with distance, so the city looks like a scale model. 2) The towers are boxy extrusions with one repeated window texture and no rooftop or facade variety. 3) The rotor is drawn as a solid ring or disc instead of motion-blurred blades. 4) The water has artifacts: smeared blur, pasted-on foam blotches, floating blur discs and streak reflections. 5) The foreground figure is mannequin-grade and staging is static. 6) Gameplay bugs are visible: pistol ammo shown while flying, an OS cursor in the minimap, a debug text line, and mission text starting in lower case. Suggested order of work: lighting and atmosphere first (directional sun with real shadows, plus height and distance fog), then rotor-blade rendering, then water foam and reflections, then facade detail and variety on the towers, and finally character fidelity. Only two B frames really impressed me: the dusk searchlight shot (pair 2) and the backlit banking helicopter (pair 1). No A frame did.
